name: Dell XE9785L 8xMI355X, MLPerf Inference v6.1 INTERACTIVE: Llama 3.1 8B while holding an inter-token latency cap
unit: output tokens/s (aggregate, harness 'Completed tokens per second')
methodology: AGGREGATE. MLPerf Inference v6.1 Closed division, Datacenter suite, INTERACTIVE scenario, stored under a directory named Interactive and published in a Scenario column reading Interactive. LOADS: Server arrival model (target_qps 0.5, min_duration 120000 ms) PLUS the Interactive category's hard inter-token bound; the MLCommons reference repo states the Interactive latency contract as ttft <= 450ms and tpot <= 40ms for this benchmark family. Batch size not a fixed published number, but bounded from above by the inter-token budget. Completed samples per second 1019.06. Model shape GEN_LEN 8127480. POWER: has_power=False, design_power_watts=null, no declared cap. OMITTED BY SOURCE: TP size, KV dtype, achieved concurrency, clock state, cooling.
notes: AUDIT WARNING ON THIS RECORD: the harness log at this path prints 'Scenario : Server' as its own header, and it reports 'Performance constraints satisfied : Yes' exactly as a Server run does. Nothing in the raw artifact identifies it as Interactive. The directory name and the summary.csv column are the only evidence. Anyone auditing MLPerf by reading raw logs - the most defensible way to audit - will silently misclassify every Interactive result in the database as a Server result. That defect is recorded as data/gotchas/bench-mlperf-interactive-scenario-labels-itself-server.json. Substantively: 130540 tok/s is 17.6% below Offline and 12.1% below Server on this same node, which is the cost of guaranteeing no user waits more than 40ms between tokens.
